sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Long County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Long County splits the work between two offices on South McDonald Street in Ludowici. The tax assessors set value and take appeals, while the tax commissioner bills and collects.

  • Long County Tax Assessor's Office: 285 S McDonald St, Ludowici, GA 31316. Open Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Phone (912) 545-9111. The office page links to the qPublic parcel search.
  • Long County Tax Commissioner: P.O. Box 628, 285 South McDonald Street, Ludowici, GA 31316. Phone 912-545-2127. Bill payment has moved to a newer site, and the old taxpayer search tab no longer takes payments.
  • Long County Board of Commissioners: 468 S. McDonald Street, Ludowici. This board adopts the county millage rate at a called meeting.

The Georgia Department of Revenue sends owners to the commissioner for bill questions and to the assessors for value, exemption and appeal questions. Start with the office that matches your question. Each will point you to the other if you pick wrong.

sections.h2: What does Long County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Long County is a rural, mostly agricultural county of about 400 square miles, with Ludowici as the county seat and only city. The county's own history page says farming once ran on cotton, then tobacco, corn, soybeans and cattle, and that pine forests and nearby paper mills shaped the timber economy.

The northern tip of the county sits inside Fort Stewart, the largest military installation east of the Mississippi River, and the post supplies civil service jobs to local residents. Altamaha Technical College runs a satellite campus in Ludowici. Long County School System runs the public schools, except on the base, where the Department of Defense Education Activity serves elementary students.

Growth is the story here. The Census Bureau counted 16,168 residents in 2020 and estimates 21,557 for July 1, 2025, a rise of 33.5% over the 2020 estimates base. QuickFacts lists 7,798 housing units, a 65.2% owner-occupied share and a median owner-occupied value of $218,300 for 2020 to 2024. Workers spend a mean 29.8 minutes getting to their jobs.

Aimar, Beards Creek, Donald and Tibet are unincorporated communities. Owners there deal with the county, not a city hall, for permits and tax. The county neighbors Liberty, McIntosh, Wayne and Tattnall counties.

sections.h2: How has the Long County tax digest changed since 2021?
sections.html:
The county's published five-year history shows a taxable base that keeps growing and a county rate that moves in steps. The net digest rose from about $328.8 million in 2021 to about $546.0 million in the 2026 figures, and the net maintenance and operation millage was 17.802 mills in the 2026 presentation.

Source: the 2026 Tax Digest and 5 Year History published by the Long County Board of Commissioners. The notice says the levy reflects reductions from Property Tax Relief Local Option Sales Tax proceeds, also called FLOST, applied against property tax. County voters authorized FLOST in 2025, and the combined sales tax rate in Long County became 9% on January 1, 2026.

For the 2025 rate, the assessors' page carried a notice of a tentative increase of 20.72 percent: a rate of 18.707 mills against 15.496 mills without the increase, with hearings on February 12 and February 19, 2026. The county then scheduled a called meeting for September 24, 2026 to adopt the 2026 millage. School and state levies are billed on top of the county figure, so read the rate on your own bill.

sections.h2: When are Long County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Long County's recent due dates have moved with the digest. For the 2025 bills, the tax commissioner's page listed real estate taxes due May 12, 2026, and mobile home taxes due June 1, 2026 instead of the usual April 1, because the digest was released late.

Georgia's baseline is a December 20 due date with 60 days from billing, and a county may set another date. Read the date printed on your bill and ask the commissioner's office when the next billing will mail.

  • Returns of property are filed between January 1 and April 1 every year.
  • Mobile home tax is normally due April 1.
  • Payments are taken through the new payment site that the commissioner's page links to.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Long County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Long County Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The state provides a uniform appeal form for the purpose.

On that first filing you choose the route: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. The Department of Revenue states that it cannot override the assessors, equalization board, hearing officer, arbitrator or Superior Court on an individual appraisal. If the county has adopted a written policy accepting electronic service, an appeal can be emailed, and the assessors' office can say whether Long County has one. The office lists longcoappr@longcountyga.gov for contact.

Appeal grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption. Pull your parcel on qPublic first and compare it with recent nearby sales before you file.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Long County?
sections.html:
The state's standard homestead exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of fair market value, according to the Department of Revenue. You qualify by owning and living in the home as your primary residence.

  • Homestead applications go to the county tax commissioner or the assessors, depending on the county. Ask which office takes them in Long County.
  • Many Georgia counties add exemptions beyond the state one. Ask the assessors for the local list and its age and income limits.
  • Farm, timber and conservation assessments rest on a covenant signed with the assessors, so ask before assuming acreage qualifies.

The Census Bureau lists 275 building permits in Long County for 2025. New construction and added improvements feed the digest, so check your January 1 value against the parcel record.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Long County tax when you sell?
sections.html:
Georgia law makes the person who owns the property on January 1 responsible for that year's full tax, even if the house sells on January 2. The Department of Revenue says there is no refund for partial-year owners, so buyer and seller settle the split in the contract.

Before closing, ask the tax commissioner for a payoff figure that includes interest or penalty, and give the closing attorney the current bill. A recorded tax lien, called a fi fa, sits on the general execution docket at the Clerk of Superior Court and has to be paid or cleared for the buyer to receive clean title.

Selling an inherited, behind-on-tax or tenant-occupied house in Long County follows the same steps. Call the commissioner early, because a figure quoted weeks ahead can change as interest adds up.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Long County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Long County Tax Commissioner at 912-545-2127 for billing and payment, and the Tax Assessor's Office at (912) 545-9111 for value, exemptions and appeals. The commissioner's mailing address is P.O. Box 628, Ludowici, GA 31316.

faqs.q: What is the Long County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and name your appeal route on that first filing.

faqs.q: Did Long County raise its millage rate?
faqs.a: The county's published history shows the net M&O millage at 14.738 in 2023, 18.707 in 2024 and 2025, and 17.802 in the 2026 presentation. Sales tax relief proceeds were applied against the levy, so ask the commissioner for the rate on your own bill.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of tax if I sell mid-year?
faqs.a: No refund exists for a partial year. The Department of Revenue says the January 1 owner owes the whole year's tax, so buyer and seller settle the split in the sales contract.

faqs.q: Where do I look up a Long County parcel online?
faqs.a: Use the qPublic property search linked from the Long County Tax Assessor's page. It shows parcel records, and the assessors' office can explain any value you see there.
